latest_release.name: NX2navi 0.9.2
latest_release.body:
## Install or update

- **Already have 0.6.0 or newer:** start the launcher; it offers 0.9.2, updates itself and keeps the game it compiled
  and the shaders it prepared. Only what changed is compiled again.
- **Already have 0.5.0:** the same, and the game's code 0.5.0 compiled is kept as it was compiled (for any x86-64
  processor); *Rebuild the Game* in the launcher's home compiles it again for yours.
- **New install:** download **`NX2navi-Setup-0.9.2.exe`** below, put it next to your `.nup` dump of the game and start
  it. Windows SmartScreen warns on the first start because the setup is not signed: choose *More info* and *Run
  anyway*. The launcher checks your game files, builds the game (10 to 25 minutes, once), prepares every shader and
  starts it.

**Requirements:** Windows 10 or 11; an x86-64 CPU with SSE4.2; 16 GB of RAM; about 30 GB free for the game and 1.5 GB
for the launcher; a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 and `VK_EXT_external_memory_host` (current NVIDIA and AMD cards). A GPU without
`VK_EXT_mesh_shader` gets the mesh shader fallback as before, or runs the game's mesh shaders as compute shaders with
`low_end_gpu = 1` (new, see below).

## New

- **An experimental mode for older graphics cards:** *Low-end GPU mode (experimental)* in the settings menu's Game
  tab, or `low_end_gpu = 1` in nx2navi.ini. It turns on a set of changes written by Tobim6 and measured on a Radeon
  RX 580. They are off by default, because they were not run by us on other cards:
  - Grass, moss and other foliage on cards without mesh shaders (AMD before RDNA 2, such as the RX 400 and 500 series
    and Vega; NVIDIA before the GTX 16 and RTX 20 series): the game's mesh shaders run as compute shaders and what
    they make is drawn as ordinary triangles.
  - Video memory kept within what the driver reports free, with 512 MB in reserve, and a texture that does not fit
    the first memory heap placed in the next one with room. Large batches of texture uploads go to the GPU early
    instead of growing until a submit runs out of memory.
  - Less waiting for the GPU: the game memory a submission needs is copied while the frame is recorded, and the game
    goes on once a frame's first submission is handed over. On the RX 580 the replay's part of that wait went from
    12 ms to 6.9, with the recording thread used on AMD cards without mesh shaders.
  - Frames prepared on a thread of their own (this one can show a dark or flickering frame now and then), and memory
    pools the game refills every frame kept in system memory.
  - A texture the game reads after another image was drawn over its memory gets memory of its own, which removed
    teal splotches from the fog of Kokiri Forest on that card.

  While the mode is on, the Game tab lists its settings underneath the switch: the video memory limit and reserve,
  the upload batch size, mesh shader emulation and its memory, foliage detail (`foliage = full`, `reduced` or `off`)
  and compiling the game's code at -O2 at the next *Rebuild the Game* (`guest_opt = 2`, a build several times
  longer). With the mode off none of them is read, also when nx2navi.ini sets one.
- **Link's own motion for DLSS, FSR 3.1 and frame generation** (`selective_motion = 1` in nx2navi.ini, off by
  default): Link and the equipment attached to him are drawn a second time with last frame's pose, so the upscaler
  gets their real motion in fast turns, attacks and jumps instead of an estimate. It has not been played by us yet. By
  automata-rtx (pull request #699).
- **A Switch used as a controller over USB** (it shows up as "Nyx Joy-Con") is taken as a gamepad. Any other joystick
  the game cannot use is named in the log once, with its ids. By Tobim6.

## Fixed

- **FSR and DLSS showed a blocky, shaking picture with the HUD hidden.** The upscaler's picture was put where the
  game draws its HUD. With the HUD off the game skips that step, and the frame's last step then drew the game'

hot_issues.title: Heavy stutter and green blocky artifacts in fog on AMD RX 6750 XT
On version 0.8.0: The missing objects do appear, but I am experiencing severe texture shimmering (a "flickering" or "lightning/storm" effect). This issue was not present in 0.7.1.

detail.readme: # NX2navi **Join the official NX2navi update discord server: https://discord.com/invite/uf6gSrsPpq** **NX2navi** is a static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* for Nintendo Switch 2 (game version 1.1.1) into a native x86-64 application for Windows, with a Vulkan renderer ([docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)). > [!IMPORTANT] > **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of the game, dumped from your own console. > Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided. > > The game is built from your files on your machine, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use. Do not share it. ## Status Early development, playable. Kokiri Forest, Kakariko Village, Death Mountain Trail and its crater, the Temple of Time and the Great Fairy fountains play at 60 fps and above on current GPUs, from the title screen and from saves. Visual bugs and occasional crashes are still expected ([Known issues](#known-issues)). Report problems as issues, following [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Features - Native code, not emulation - 60 fps by default, or a limit of 30 to 240 fps, the display's refresh rate or unlimited - Native widescreen and ultrawide (the window's shape, 21:9 or 32:9) with the HUD, menus and movies kept 16:9 - Game resolutions from 1080p to above the game's 1440p: 1800p, 4K, 5K or the window's own size, sharp on high-DPI displays - Upscaling and anti-aliasing: NVIDIA DLSS (DLAA, Quality, Balanced, Performance, Ultra Performance; RTX GPUs) or AMD FSR 3.1 (Native AA and the same modes; any GPU) or AMD FSR 4 (the same modes; Radeon RX 6000, RX 7000 and RX 9000 GPUs), which render the 3D scene at the mode's share and keep the HUD sharp; or AMD FSR 1 or bilinear scaling to the window, with a sharpness setting; black bars or stretch - Frame generation: NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation (RTX 40 and 50 GPUs, paced with Reflex) at 2x, or 3x and 4x on RTX 50 GPUs (one, two or three generated frames for every frame the game draws), or AMD FSR 3.1 (any GPU), a generated frame between every two the game draws, with the HUD kept out of it, for about twice the frame rate on a fast display; in a window of another shape than the picture, frames are generated inside the picture only, so the black bars stay clean. The frame limit counts the frames the game draws, and frame generation adds its frames on top of it. The frame limit can also be handed to RivaTuner Statistics Server - HDR on HDR displays, two kinds: the game's scene tone mapped to the display's peak, matched to the game's mid grey and tone, with true blacks, or the game's own native HDR; peak, game and HUD brightness in the menu - The game's known shaders prepared when the game is built, and the pipelines met in play built again in the background at each start, so play rarely stops to compile them; a shader or pipeline met for the first time can still hold a frame, and a draw that must wait for its pipeline has it built on worker threads, never on the game's drawing thread - In-game settings menu (F1, or Minus and Plus together on a gamepad) and performance overlay (F10) - Keyboard, mouse and gamepads with remapping, Nintendo, Xbox or PlayStation button layout, rumble and gyro; the game follows whichever connected gamepad you press, and DualShock 3 controllers are read directly when enabled - Xbox, PlayStation, Steam Deck and keyboard and mouse button prompts in the game's own text, drawn on your PC when the game is built; the keyboard prompts follow your key bindings - Stereo or 5.1 surround sound output, on the output device of your choice; the default microphone for the game's microphone input - The monitor the game opens on, straight in fullscreen when fullscreen is on - Your Discord status shows "Playing NX2navi" with the play time (on by default; the Game tab of the menu or the launcher's Settings turns it off) - Docked or handheld console mode - The game's textures stay compressed (BC3, about half the video memory at the same speed) unless the PC has 20 GiB of video memory and 48 GiB of RAM, as Windows counts video memory against the system's commit limit ## Installing Download `NX2navi-Setup-.exe` from the releases and start it next to your `.nup` dump. It is the only file you need. The launcher it installs finds the dump, downloads the build tools, builds the game on your PC (20 to 45 minutes, once) and starts it; afterwards it keeps the port up to date and rebuilds only what changed ([docs/launcher.md](docs/launcher.md)). [docs/README-BuildKit.md](docs/README-BuildKit.md) describes the same build by hand, [docs/building.md](docs/building.md) building from source. Settings are in the in-game menu and in `nx2navi.ini` ([nx2navi.ini.example](nx2navi.ini.example) lists every key). Controls: [docs/controls.md](docs/controls.md). Requirements: Windows 10 or later; an x86-64 CPU with SSE4.2 (AVX2/FMA machines get a faster build); 16 GB of RAM; about 34 GB free for the game and 1.5 GB for the launcher and its tools; a GPU with Vulkan 1.3, `VK_EXT_external_memory_host` and `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`. The setup is not signed, so SmartScreen warns on its first start. ## Known issues - The first start after an install or update, and the first visit to an area, can pause briefly while the graphics driver builds what it has not seen; later starts are smooth. - Machines with 16 GB of RAM can run out of system memory in Hyrule Field. - Integrated AMD GPUs can fail at the title screen (their host memory heap is too small for the game's memory). - A rare crash in the game's particle code. ## License The source is public to read. Its additions and changes are all rights reserved ([LICENSE-ADDITIONS](LICENSE-ADDITIONS)): no part of them may be copied or published without written permission. The base import stays under its [MIT License](LICENSE), and third-party code keeps its own license ([THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)). No license grants anything for Nintendo's game. NX2navi is an independent, non-commercial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. *The Legend of Zelda*, *Ocarina of Time* and *Nintendo Switch* are trademarks of Nintendo. ## Building from source [docs/building.md](docs/building.md) lists the toolchain and the steps. `tools/make_game.py` also builds the game natively on Linux ([docs/README-BuildKit.md](docs/README-BuildKit.md), "Linux"); the launcher and the setup are Windows only. Everything the build writes stays under `build\` and `generated\`, which git ignores, as it does the runtime's shaders the build compiles (`runtime\*_spv.h`; the repository holds their source only); run `tools/check_content.py` before a commit.
